subject: Next steps: masking trace IDs & cookies in request/response logs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna.park@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-16T13:05:00-04:00
Subject: Next steps: masking trace IDs & cookies in request/response logs

Hi Anna,

Great to meet today — thanks for the detailed walkthrough of ClearWave's ingestion flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary from our call:
- You need request/response logging for debugging and audit, but logs must not expose PII or session cookies.
- Trace identifiers (trace_id / x-request-id) should not be reversible to a patient or user identity.
- Retention goal: ~90 days for log artifacts, stored only in the US; sensitive subsets may need shorter retention.
- You asked whether redaction is done inline or can be streamed to an isolated log store.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you share a 1–2 MB sample of typical request/response logs (strip patient PHI) so we can validate regex and field rules?
2) Confirm whether you prefer: a) full removal of Cookie/Set-Cookie headers, or b) pseudonymize cookie values with keyed-hash?
3) Confirm any required KMS/HSM policies (we support customer-managed keys).

Proposed Redwood approach (high level):
- Strip Cookie/Set-Cookie headers by default. Option to pseudonymize via HMAC if you need session correlation.
- Pseudonymize trace IDs with a salted HMAC truncated to 12 hex chars (non-reversible).
- Field-level redaction for known PII keys (email, ssn, patient_id) plus configurable regexes.
- Retention policies per-customer, region-limited storage for logs, and audit trails for access.

I'll attach a short draft redaction policy for your review. If you can drop the sample logs, I can have our infra team validate the detection rules and provide a small proof-of-concept (logs-in / sanitized-logs-out) by EOD Friday.

Next step: please send the sample log and your security contact for the SOC2/KMS items. Happy to hop on a 30-min tech follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Anna Park <anna.park@clearwavehealth.com>

Date: 2025-07-16T14:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: masking trace IDs & cookies in request/response logs

Ben — thanks for the recap and action items. Confirming a few specifics: 

Clarifications: 
- We do want request and response bodies for support (headers + payload), but any PHI fields (patient_name, patient_ssn, patient_email, address) must be redacted before storage.
- Cookies: we would prefer cookies removed entirely from logs. We can correlate sessions via our own session service; we don't want session tokens in any stored logs.
- Trace IDs: we want trace IDs pseudonymized so we can join events across services but cannot map back to the original ID. A keyed-hash approach is preferred.
- Retention: 90 days for general logs stored in US only (us-east-1). Shorter retention (30 days) for any logs that contain sensitive key material.

I attached a sanitized sample log snippet (we'll also send a larger sample via secure upload). For the sample you'll see typical headers and a JSON payload with patient fields.

Questions for you: 
1) Is pseudonymization done synchronously at ingest time or as a separate pipeline step? We prefer ingest-time redaction so raw sensitive data never persists in any intermediate store.
2) Can you support a customer-managed key (KMS) for the hashing salt?
3) What metrics/SLAs can you guarantee for redaction latency per request (we aim for <50ms extra in the critical path).

Security contact: David Chou (david.chou@clearwavehealth.com) will handle the SOC2/KMS questionnaire.

Thanks — Anna
Director, Platform Engineering | ClearWave Health
anna.park@clearwavehealth.com

Attachment: sample_request_log.txt (sanitized snippet)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna.park@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-16T15:00:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: masking trace IDs & cookies in request/response logs

Anna — great, thanks for the sample and the clear preference on cookies and trace IDs. Looping in Marissa (solutions lead) and Tessa (infra/ops) to scope a short technical validation.

Quick answers to your questions: 
- Redaction model: Redwood supports both inline (synchronous) redaction at ingress and an async pipeline. For ClearWave's requirement (raw never persisted), we recommend inline redaction at the edge so sensitive fields are removed/pseudonymized before any persistent buffer. That path is supported; we can show a POC.
- KMS: yes — we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS). The HMAC salt used for pseudonymization can be wrapped by your KMS; access is auditable.
- Latency impact: our typical inline redaction adds ~10–30ms on average depending on payload size and number of regex rules; we'll run your sample to produce a concrete profile. Our SLA targets for Dedicated customers include performance regression guarantees and a test harness to validate end-to-end latency.

Proposed technical approach (outline):
1) Edge agent inspects incoming HTTP(s) request and applies header rules: remove Cookie/Set-Cookie; remove Authorization headers except allowlist tokens.
2) Pseudonymize trace ids via HMAC-SHA256(salt, trace_id) truncated to 12 hex characters stored as trace_id_pseudonym.
3) Body PII detection via a combined field-rule + regex engine (configurable ruleset we can ship with ClearWave defaults).
4) Inline write to controlled log bucket in us-east-1 with retention policy applied (90 / 30 day tiers). Raw payloads never written if inline enabled.

I'll attach a draft redaction policy (PDF) for your security team to review.

Action items we can own this week:
- Tessa will run your sample against our inline redaction to produce a sanitized output and latency numbers by Friday EOD.
- Marissa will prepare a short SOW outline for Dedicated vs Hosted with redaction controls.

If that's acceptable, David can send the larger sample via secure upload and we'll get started.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: David Chou <david.chou@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Anna Park <anna.park@clearwavehealth.com>
Date: 2025-07-16T16:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: masking trace IDs & cookies in request/response logs

Ben / Anna — sending the larger sample bundle via secure upload (link in separate email). Attached here is a short snippet (sample_request_log.txt) to illustrate our typical headers/body. A couple of follow-ups from Security: 

- PHI: ClearWave is handling PHI in some pipelines (not all). For PHI flows, we require inline redaction at ingress and retention limits enforced automatically.
- KMS: we require key usage logs and key rotation policies; we'll include exact requirements in the questionnaire.
- Synchronous vs async: Security prefers synchronous inline redaction for PHI; for non-PHI flows async is acceptable.

Operational questions for Redwood: 
1) Can you provide an SOW and a ballpark price delta for Dedicated capacity that includes inline redaction (we expect high QPS during business hours)?
2) Who will own the monitoring playbook if redaction rules fail (alerts, rollbacks, & runbook)?
3) For joining traces across services after pseudonymization, can you support a deterministic HMAC (same salt) across multiple hosts? We need trace continuity for debugging but still non-reversible IDs.

We'll fill out the SOC2/KMS questionnaire but want to see the SOW first. Looking forward to the POC results.

Thanks,
David Chou
Head of Security Engineering | ClearWave Health
david.chou@clearwavehealth.com

Anna / David — thanks for the details and the sample. Short, actionable plan from Redwood side: 

1) By Friday EOD (2025-07-18) — Tessa will run your sample through inline redaction and provide: sanitized output, CPU/latency profile, and a short log of redaction rules applied.
2) By next Wednesday (2025-07-23) — Solutions will share an SOW draft with two options: Hosted (with inline redaction + retention controls) and Dedicated (reserved capacity + performance guarantees + KMS integration).
3) Security questionnaire — David, once you share the questionnaire, we'll have a Security engineer respond within 3 business days.

Short notes on determinism: deterministic HMAC with a customer-managed key is supported for trace continuity; we will document rotation implications (rotation requires re-hashing strategy for historical joins).

Please confirm the above timeline and whether you want an on-site (virtual) tech review during the POC run.

Regards,
